claims.statement: Emotional well-being rises with log income but there is no further progress beyond an annual income of about $75,000, while life evaluation continues to rise.
claims.scope: More than 450,000 responses to the Gallup-Healthways Well-Being Index, US, 2008-2009; dichotomous yes/no items about yesterday's emotions.

our_assessment.why: Read in full 2026-10-17. The $75,000 is an inference chain, not an estimate: the top two income groups 'do not differ', so satiation must lie 'somewhere in the third category from the top' ($60-90k), whence 'beyond about $75,000/y, there is no improvement whatever'. The first link reads a borderline non-significant step as zero: for positive affect the top step is +0.0035 (t = 1.9, p ~ .06, n ~ 113,000), 43% of the step below, with a 95% CI reaching 87% of it (k1_satiation_ci.py). Blue affect flattens more convincingly (CI excludes more than 42% of the previous step). The items are yes/no reports about yesterday, averaged into fractions -- the ceiling structure kkm2023-conflict-resolved#c2 builds on is in the paper's own definitions. Correct reading: emotional well-being gains SHRINK markedly above ~$75k on these dichotomous items; 'no improvement whatever' is not what Table 2 can show. This now supports kkm2023#c2 on evidence, not only argument.

checked.how: six routes: (1) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2944762/pdf/ -> 1,817 B of HTML; (2) https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC2944762/fullTextXML -> HTTP 200 with a ZERO-BYTE body; (3) https://www.pnas.org/doi/pdf/10.1073/pnas.1011492107 -> Cloudflare interstitial; (4) https://europepmc.org/articles/pmc2944762?pdf=render -> 403 on /api/getPdf; (5) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2944762/pdf/pnas.201011492.pdf -> 1,817 B of HTML; (6) NCBI OA service oa.fcgi -> 404, the endpoint is retired.
checked.result: NOT RETRIEVABLE from this box. Unpaywall reports is_oa = true, oa_status = green, with exactly one location: the PMC record, which is the one that serves an interstitial. So the paper is free to read by a human with a browser and unavailable to any automated agent -- a state no availability metric in existence distinguishes from open. Semantic Scholar's openAccessPdf field points at route (4), which 403s. That is worth its own line: THREE independent open-access indexes assert this PDF is available and none of the URLs they give returns a PDF.

relations.why: Reciprocal: KKM qualifies this paper. Note the KKM footnote -- Angus Deaton did not participate in the adversarial collaboration and should not be taken as endorsing its conclusions.
